text:
Recent work supports text-enriched sequential recommendation, but provides limited direct evidence for a small text encoder trained from scratch inside GRU4Rec. [UniSRec (2023)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.13731) learns transferable language representations through pretraining and finetuning. [ITS-Rec (2025)](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/9/1748) integrates titles, descriptions and reviews with IDs, but uses pretrained BERT and a SASRec backbone; reviews contribute its largest gains, limiting applicability here. [Sequence-level Semantic Representation Fusion (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.18166) specifically warns that directly adding text and ID embeddings can be ineffective because their characteristics differ.

Semantic similarity is insufficient evidence of complementarity. [SComGNN (AAAI 2024)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28734) emphasizes that complements combine relevance with dissimilarity: a phone and earbuds may be purchased successively despite differing attributes. Its graph-based results support distinguishing complementary relationships from generic similarity, but do not establish that title/description encoding alone discovers them.

Practical hypothesis, rather than a demonstrated result: jointly train a compact token embedding–pooling–projection encoder with item IDs and the GRU next-item objective, using a learned gate to control text contribution. Shared tokens could help sparse items, while interaction supervision and distinct context/candidate projections could learn directional purchasing relationships without forcing successive products to be semantically similar. Keep all components within one jointly trained category model; assess improvement against the ID-only baseline using the fixed macro validation HR@10. The located papers do not establish gains for this exact from-scratch GRU configuration.
